issues.problem: Near/far planes come from the garden yaml (MipNeRF360 loader, APPLY_PCA_RESCALE false). The NeRFICG TanksAndTemples_3DGS loader defaults to APPLY_PCA_RESCALE=True with NEAR_PLANE 0.01 in rescaled units, so the paper's T&T/DB near plane is not pinned by the released code.
issues.evidence: source/nerficg/src/Datasets/TanksAndTemples_3DGS.py:21-28 vs fastergs_garden.yaml NEAR_PLANE 0.2. 3DGS also culls at z<=0.2 world units, so 0.2 is a defensible 3DGS-equivalent choice.
issues.fix: Note it as an ambiguity in report.md, with 0.2 world units = 3DGS in_frustum. No code change needed.

issues.problem: The profile does not measure what the paper's timing tables report. Tab. 1/2 give end-to-end 30k training time and peak VRAM against official 3DGS. The profile gives per-phase ms (forward/backward/update) on the final checkpoint against gsplat with torch Adam. It leaves out ADC, Morton, sorting growth over training and fused-ssim. The noise is large: the identical loss takes 10.7 ms in one path and 18.3 ms in the other in profile-smoke-1.json.
issues.evidence: evidence/profile-smoke-1.json loss_ms 10.73 vs 18.33 for the same loss; paper Tab. 2 reports training time only.
issues.fix: Label the profile as a per-phase kernel comparison against gsplat, not a reproduction of Tab. 1/2's 3.1-4.6x. Repeat it (or interleave paths) and report the spread. If a speed number is wanted, also report bench wall-time ratios from same-GPU runs.

issues.problem: Probe thresholds are 2-3 orders of magnitude looser than the measured errors. Measured: update 1.1e-5, v 2.9e-5, image 1.3e-6, grads <=1.4e-6. The probes still catch removal (SGD and dense-reference checks), but a subtle regression of up to ~1e-3 would pass.
issues.evidence: ss-verify rerun: fastergs-adam update_rel_err 1.10e-5, exp_avg_sq 2.92e-5; render grads ~1e-6.
issues.fix: Tighten to ~1e-4 (Adam) and ~1e-4 / 1e-4 (render), or note the margin.

issues.problem: No probe checks that the opacity reset zeroes the opacity moments while keeping step, or that state['step'] survives densify/prune/permute. Checked by hand here (see summary), but nothing guards it.
issues.evidence: Independent check: FusedAdam vs torch Adam through append, permute, reset_opa and remove. 16 steps on both sides, param rel err <=4e-7, m 3e-7, v 2e-5.
issues.fix: Add a reset step to fastergs-adc, asserting opacity moments are zero, step is unchanged and opacities are clamped to logit(0.01).

issues.problem: The smoke comparison (23.42 vs 22.99, 65 s vs 150 s) is confounded and is not fidelity evidence. Black vs white background, opacity lr 0.025 vs 0.05, 2k steps, a shared GPU, and only one scene (garden), which is not in the benchmark set.
issues.evidence: report.md smoke table; baseline gsplat config differs (CLAUDE.md, plan gap 5).
issues.fix: State that the smoke run is a sanity check only.

issues.problem: Our gsplat baselines are 0.41 (T&T 23.36 vs 23.77) and 0.53 dB (DB 29.28 vs 29.81) below the paper's 3DGS row. They also differ in background and opacity lr. So 'delta vs our baseline ~ 0' and 'absolute = 23.75/29.78' are different criteria, and an exact port could plausibly land between them.
issues.evidence: runs/baseline3dgs-tandt-30000 truck 25.21 / train 21.52; runs/baseline3dgs-db-30000 drjohnson 28.76 / playroom 29.80; paper_results.json.
issues.fix: Say in advance which criterion is primary (paper absolute ±0.5 dB), and interpret any gain over our baseline in light of the bg/opacity-lr differences.

issues.problem: Official training_cleanup also re-applies the Morton sort after the final prune. This is omitted. It has no quality effect and only matters for inference speed/memory layout.
issues.fix: Optional: call self.morton after the final prune.

issues.problem: The report omits that LPIPS is VGG on [-1,1]. That matches NeRFICG (torchmetrics normalize=True, vgg) and the paper, but not the 3DGS paper (which explains 0.204 vs 3DGS-paper 0.183 on T&T). Gap 8 says 'paper: unspecified'; it is in fact specified by the NeRFICG code.
issues.fix: Update gap 8: LPIPS-VGG on [-1,1] matches the official evaluation.

Kernel instance count equals the lower bound of tiles holding visible fragments (27 vs AABB 100, 3-sigma 100). Removing exact culling or opacity-aware bounds raises n, and over-culling drops it below L.

summary: Approved: 0 critical, 0 major, 8 minor. The pinned configuration is the paper's headline 'Ours' row, which equals Tab. 2/3 'Full'. Tab. 3 lists '+ fused updates' (24.73) and '+ skip invisible' (24.59) as optional additions on top of Full (24.72), and the main branch has no fused path. Excluding both is correct. Every training hyper-parameter matches Trainer.py/Model.py defaults: ADC 600..14900 every 100, inclusive callbacks; prune-large only when iteration > 3000; resets 3000..12000 with moments zeroed and step kept; no extra reset at 500 with a black background; Morton at 0/5k/10k/15k with priority order ADC > Morton > reset; opacity lr 0.025; lr for the other fields; extent 1.1x max camera distance; SfM init with opacity 0.1 and RMS 3-NN scales; SH +1 per 1000. The official code ships only a garden yaml, so T&T/DB use the loader defaults. Both datasets are the 3DGS-provided pre-downscaled images (979x546, 980x545, 1332x876, 1264x832), which matches our native data and the paper's 'pre-downscaled when provided'. Step mapping (official 0-based callback i == runtime after_backward(s=i)) is correct, including info accumulation up to step 14900. Vendored rasterization/adam/utils are byte-identical to FasterGSCudaBackend @ 090e8ad. bindings.cpp only drops filter3d/MCMC, and the official setup.py flags are used. Reruns on GPU 3: 7 unit tests pass; ss-verify passes all 8 probes (image 1.28e-6, grads <=1.1e-6, info 7.5e-7, Adam 1.1e-5). An independent check ran FusedAdam vs torch Adam through append, permute, reset_opa and remove for 16 steps on both: step counts equal, params <=4e-7, moments <=2e-5. Baselines are confirmed at 23.36/29.28, and the paper targets in paper_results.json match Tab. 1. Main caveats are interpretive. The profile is a per-phase kernel comparison against gsplat, not the paper's end-to-end training-time table, and it is noisy (the same loss differs 1.7x between paths). The smoke result is confounded by bg/opacity-lr differences. Our baseline sits 0.4-0.5 dB below the paper's 3DGS row, so the absolute and delta criteria differ.
